title: The Mongoose with the Half Golden Body
text:
After the great war, King Yudhishthira performed a magnificent horse sacrifice. Gold, food and gifts poured out to priests and the poor. When it was over, a mongoose appeared on the sacrificial ground. Half of its body shone like gold. It rolled in the ground, then declared in a human voice that this whole sacrifice was not equal to a handful of barley flour given by a poor brahmin of Kurukshetra.

Asked to explain, the mongoose told its story. During a famine a brahmin lived with his wife, son and daughter-in-law by gleaning grain. After days of hunger they had gathered just enough barley to make four small portions. As they were about to eat, a hungry guest arrived. The brahmin gave him his share. The guest was still hungry, so the wife gave hers, then the son, then the daughter-in-law.

The guest then revealed himself as Dharma, and the family was taken up to heaven. The mongoose came out of its hole, rolled in the flour that had fallen, and wherever it touched, its fur turned to gold.

Ever since, it had searched for a sacrifice that could gild its other half. Yudhishthira's had not done it.
lesson: A gift's worth lies in what it costs the giver and the spirit behind it. Sharing your little in a hard time can mean more than giving plenty from abundance.
people: A mongoose, Yudhishthira, a poor brahmin family
